question:
CQ:A = 4 + 44 + 444 + ……and
S = 2(3x - 5)^{-1} + 4(3x - 5)^{-2} + 8(3x - 5)^{-3} + ……are two infinite series.
Combining Chapters 5 & 7 [1766667948730]
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Find out the nature and type of the roots of \(2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0\).","marks":0,"answer":"Given equation, \(2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0\)
Discriminant, D = \(7^2 - 4 \times 2 \times 3 = 49 - 24 = 25 = 5^2\)
Here, the discriminant of the equation, D > 0 and is a perfect square number.
Roots of the equation are rational, unequal, and real numbers (Ans.)"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Find the sum of the first n terms of the series A.","marks":0,"answer":"Given that, A = 4 + 44 + 444 + ………...
= 4(1 + 11 + 111 + ……….. + nth term)
= \(\frac{4}{9}\) (9 + 99 + 999 + ……….. + nth term)
= \(\frac{4}{9}\) ((10 - 1) + (100 - 1) + (1000 - 1) + …… + nth term)
= \(\frac{4}{9}\) ((10 + 100 + 1000 + ……… + nth term) - n)
= \(\frac{4}{9}\) (10 \(\cdot\) \(\left(\frac{10^n - 1}{10 - 1}\right)\) - n)
= \(\frac{40}{81}\) (10^n - 1) - \(\frac{4}{9}\) n
Therefore, the sum of the first n terms of series A,
\[S_n = \frac{40}{81}(10^n - 1) - \frac{4}{9} n \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Impose a condition on x under which the infinite series S will have a sum (to infinity) and find that sum.","marks":0,"answer":"Given, series:
\[S = 2(3x - 5)^{-1} + 4(3x - 5)^{-2} + 8(3x - 5)^{-3} + ……...\]
= \(\frac{2}{3x - 5} + \frac{4}{(3x - 5)^2} + \frac{8}{(3x - 5)^3} + ……\) which is a geometric series.
The first term of the series, a = \(\frac{2}{3x - 5}\)
Common ratio, r = \(\frac{4/(3x-5)^2}{2/(3x-5)} = \frac{2}{3x - 5}\)
The series will have sum to infinity if \(|r| < 1\)
Therefore, \(\left|\frac{2}{3x - 5}\right| < 1\) or, \(-1 < \frac{2}{3x - 5} < 1\)
Either, \(\frac{2}{3x - 5} < 1\) or, \(\frac{2}{3x - 5} > -1\)
or, \(2 < 3x - 5\) or, \(2 > -(3x - 5)\)
or, \(3x - 5 > 2\) or, \(3x - 5 < -2\)
or, \(3x > 7\) or, \(3x < 3\)
∴ \(x > \frac{7}{3}\) or \(x < 1\)
Required condition: \(x > \frac{7}{3}\) or, \(x < 1\) (Ans.)
Sum to infinity, \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r} = \frac{\frac{2}{3x - 5}}{1 - \frac{2}{3x - 5}}\)
= \(\frac{2}{3x - 5} \div \frac{3x - 5 - 2}{3x - 5} = \frac{2}{3x - 5} \times \frac{3x - 5}{3x - 7} = \frac{2}{3x - 7}\) (Ans.)
---"}]

question: CQ:\[\frac{1}{3x+5}+\frac{1}{(3x+5)^2}+\frac{1}{(3x+5)^3}+....\] is an infinite geometric series.
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Express 0.05 (with repeating 5) as rational fraction.","marks":0,"answer":"0.05 (with repeating 5) = 0.05555 ......
= 0.05 + 0.005 + 0.0005 + ......
\(1^{\text{st}}\) term of the infinite series, a = 0.05
Common ratio, r = \(\frac{0.005}{0.05}=0.1<1\)
So, 0.05 = \(\frac{0.05}{1-0.1}=\frac{0.05}{0.9}=\frac{5}{90}=\frac{1}{18}\) (Ans.)"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"If \(x = \frac{2}{3}\), then find the series and sum up to the first \(10^{th}\) terms of the series.","marks":0,"answer":"For \(x = \frac{2}{3}\), the given series can be described by
\[\frac{1}{2+5}+\frac{1}{(2+5)^2}+\frac{1}{(2+5)^3}+......\]
\[= \frac{1}{7}+\frac{1}{7^2}+\frac{1}{7^3}+......\]
Here, \(1^{\text{st}}\) term of this series, a = \(\frac{1}{7}\)
Common ratio, r = \(\frac{1/7^2}{1/7}=\frac{1}{7}<1\)
So, sum up to first n terms = \(\frac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}\)
∴ Sum up to first 10 terms = \(\frac{\frac{1}{7}\left(1-\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)^{10}\right)}{1-\frac{1}{7}}\)
\[= \frac{\frac{1}{7}\left(1-\frac{1}{7^{10}}\right)}{\frac{6}{7}} = \frac{1}{6}\left(1-\frac{1}{7^{10}}\right) = \frac{1}{6}\left(\frac{7^{10}-1}{7^{10}}\right) \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"If the series has sum up to infinity, then what condition should be imposed upon x? Determine that sum.","marks":0,"answer":"Given,
The series is \(\frac{1}{3x+5}+\frac{1}{(3x+5)^2}+\frac{1}{(3x+5)^3}+......\)
\(1^{\text{st}}\) term of the series, a = \(\frac{1}{3x+5}\)
Common ratio, r = \(\frac{1/(3x+5)^2}{1/(3x+5)} = \frac{1}{3x+5}\)
Sum up to infinity will exist, if |r|<1
That is, \(\left|\frac{1}{3x+5}\right|<1\)
or, -1 < \(\frac{1}{3x+5}\)<1
Either, \(\frac{1}{3x+5}<1\) or, \(\frac{1}{3x+5}>-1\)
or, \(3x+5>1\) or, \(3x+5<-1\)
or, \(3x+5-5>1-5\) or, \(3x+5-5<-1-5\)
or, \(3x>-4\) or, \(3x<-6\)
∴ \(x > \frac{-4}{3}\) or, \(x < \frac{-6}{3}\)
∴ \(x < -2\)
∴ Sum up to infinity of the series will exist if \(x > \frac{-4}{3}\) or \(x < -2\) (Ans.)
Now sum up to infinity of the series,
\[S_{\infty} = \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{\frac{1}{3x+5}}{1-\frac{1}{3x+5}} = \frac{\frac{1}{3x+5}}{\frac{3x+5-1}{3x+5}} = \frac{1}{3x+4} \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]
---"}]

question:
CQ:(i) 3(1 + 11 + 111 + ………..)
(ii) a + ap + ap^2 + ………is a geometric series.
Combining Chapters 5 & 7
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Find the discriminant of equation \(7x - 1 + 2x^2 = 0\).","marks":0,"answer":"Given equation, \(7x - 1 + 2x^2 = 0\)
or, \(2x^2 + 7x - 1 = 0\);
Comparing the equation with ax^2 + bx + c = 0, we get,
a = 2, b = 7 and c = -1
Discriminant of the equation, D = \(b^2 - 4ac\)
= \(7^2 - 4 \times 2 \times (-1)\)
= \(49 + 8 = 57\) (Ans.)"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Find the sum of the first n terms of the series no. (i).","marks":0,"answer":"Given series: 3(1 + 11 + 111 + ……….. + nth term)
= \(\frac{3}{9}\) (9 + 99 + 999 + ……….. + nth term)
= \(\frac{1}{3}\) ((10 - 1) + (100 - 1) + (1000 - 1) + …… + nth term)
= \(\frac{1}{3}\) ((10 + 100 + 1000 + ……… + nth term) - n)
= \(\frac{1}{3}\) (10 \(\cdot\) \(\left(\frac{10^n - 1}{10 - 1}\right)\) - n)
= \(\frac{1}{3}\) (\(\frac{10(10^n - 1)}{9}\) - n)
= \(\frac{10}{27}(10^n - 1) - \frac{n}{3}\)
Therefore, the sum of the first n terms is: \(S_n = \frac{10}{27}(10^n - 1) - \frac{n}{3}\) (Ans.)"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"If a = p = \(\frac{1}{2x + 3}\), then impose a condition on x under which the infinite series will have a sum to infinity and find that sum.","marks":0,"answer":"Given a = p = \(\frac{1}{2x + 3}\).
The infinite geometric series is: \(a + ap + ap^2 + …… = \frac{1}{2x+3} + \left(\frac{1}{2x+3}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{1}{2x+3}\right)^3 + ……\)
First term, \(a = \frac{1}{2x + 3}\)
Common ratio, \(r = \frac{1}{2x + 3}\)
The series will have a sum to infinity if \(|r| < 1\), i.e., \(\left|\frac{1}{2x + 3}\right| < 1\).
This implies \(-1 < \frac{1}{2x + 3} < 1\).
Solving:
From \(\frac{1}{2x + 3} < 1\): \(\frac{1}{2x + 3} - 1 < 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{1 - (2x+3)}{2x+3} < 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{-2x -2}{2x+3} < 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{x+1}{2x+3} > 0\).
From \(\frac{1}{2x + 3} > -1\): \(\frac{1}{2x + 3} + 1 > 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{1 + (2x+3)}{2x+3} > 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{2x+4}{2x+3} > 0\).
Combining the conditions, the required condition is: \(x < -\frac{3}{2}\) or \(x > -1\).
Sum to infinity, \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r} = \frac{\frac{1}{2x+3}}{1 - \frac{1}{2x+3}} = \frac{\frac{1}{2x+3}}{\frac{2x+3-1}{2x+3}} = \frac{1}{2x+2} = \frac{1}{2(x+1)}\) (Ans.)
---"}]

subject: Higher Mathematics
question: CQ:\[\frac{1}{3x+1}+\frac{1}{(3x+1)^2}+\frac{1}{(3x+1)^3}+......\] is an infinite geometric series.
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"If \(x=1\), find the common ratio of the series.","marks":0,"answer":"Given series,
\[\frac{1}{3x+1}+\frac{1}{(3x+1)^2}+\frac{1}{(3x+1)^3}+......\]
Here, common ratio, \( r=\frac{1/(3x+1)^2}{1/(3x+1)}=\frac{1}{3x+1} \)
If \(x=1\), then \(r=\frac{1}{3\times1+1}=\frac{1}{3+1}=\frac{1}{4} \quad \text{(Ans.)}\)"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"If \(x=\frac{2}{3}\), then find the sum of the first 10 terms of the series.","marks":0,"answer":"From ‘a’ we get, common ratio, \( r=\frac{1}{3x+1} \)
From the given series we get, first term, \( a=\frac{1}{3x+1} \)
For \(x=\frac{2}{3}, a=\frac{1}{3\times \frac{2}{3}+1}=\frac{1}{2+1}=\frac{1}{3} \)
and \( r=\frac{1}{3\times \frac{2}{3}+1}=\frac{1}{2+1}=\frac{1}{3}<1 \)
Now, the sum of the first 10 terms of the series,
\[S_{10}=\frac{a(1-r^{10})}{1-r}=\frac{\frac{1}{3}\left(1-\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{10}\right)}{1-\frac{1}{3}}\]
\[= \frac{\frac{1}{3}\left(1-\frac{1}{3^{10}}\right)}{\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{3^{10}}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3^{10}-1}{3^{10}}\right) \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Impose a condition on ‘x’ under which the given infinite series will have a sum and find that sum.","marks":0,"answer":"The series will have a sum to infinity if \(|r| < 1\), i.e., \(\left|\frac{1}{3x+1}\right| < 1\).
This implies \(-1 < \frac{1}{3x+1} < 1\).
Solving:
From \(\frac{1}{3x+1} < 1\): \(\frac{1}{3x+1} - 1 < 0 \Rightarrow \frac{1 - (3x+1)}{3x+1} < 0 \Rightarrow \frac{-3x}{3x+1} < 0 \Rightarrow \frac{x}{3x+1} > 0\).
From \(\frac{1}{3x+1} > -1\): \(\frac{1}{3x+1} + 1 > 0 \Rightarrow \frac{1 + (3x+1)}{3x+1} > 0 \Rightarrow \frac{3x+2}{3x+1} > 0\).
Combining the conditions, the required condition is: \(x < -\frac{2}{3}\) or \(x > 0\).
Sum to infinity, \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r} = \frac{\frac{1}{3x+1}}{1 - \frac{1}{3x+1}} = \frac{\frac{1}{3x+1}}{\frac{3x+1-1}{3x+1}} = \frac{1}{3x}\) (Ans.)
---"}]

subject: Higher Mathematics
question:
CQ:(i) \(X=8+88+888+…\)
(ii) \(Y=5+\frac{10}{3}+\frac{20}{9}+…\)
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Determine the 9th term of the sequence 1, \(\frac{2}{3}\), \(\frac{4}{9}\), \(\frac{8}{27}\)......","marks":0,"answer":"Given sequence,
\[1,\frac{2}{3},\frac{4}{9},\frac{8}{27}\]
\[\Rightarrow 1,\left(\frac{2}{3}\right),\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2,\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3\]
Which will make a geometric series.
The first term of the sequence, a = 1 and the common ratio, r = \(\frac{2}{3}\)
The 9th term of the sequence = ar\(^{9-1}\) = 1 \(\cdot\) \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^8\)
\[= \frac{256}{6561} \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Determine the sum of first n terms of the series X.","marks":0,"answer":"Given series,
\[X=8+88+888+…\]
\[= 8\left(1+11+111+…+n^{th}\text{ term}\right)\]
\[= \frac{8}{9}(9+99+999+…+n^{th}\text{ term})\]
\[= \frac{8}{9}\left((10-1)+(100-1)+(1000-1)+...+n^{th}\text{ term}\right)\]
\[= \frac{8}{9}\left((10+100+1000+...+10^n)-n\right)\]
\[= \frac{8}{9}\left(10\times\frac{10^n-1}{10-1}-n\right)\]
\[= \frac{80}{81}\left(10^n-1\right)-\frac{8n}{9}\]
The sum of the first n terms of the series
\[X=\frac{80}{81}\left(10^n-1\right)-\frac{8n}{9} \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Calculating general term of Y, determine the sum up to infinity (if exists).","marks":0,"answer":"The series of the stem (ii),
\[Y=5+\frac{10}{3}+\frac{20}{9}+…\]
\(\frac{2^{nd}\text{ term}}{1^{st}\text{ term}} = \frac{10/3}{5} = \frac{2}{3}\)
\(\frac{3^{rd}\text{ term}}{2^{nd}\text{ term}} = \frac{20/9}{10/3} = \frac{2}{3}\)
So, the common ratio is constant r = \(\frac{2}{3}\).
This is a geometric series with first term a = 5 and common ratio r = \(\frac{2}{3}\).
General term of the series = ar\(^{n-1}\) = 5\(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{n-1}\) (Ans.)
Since \(|r| = \frac{2}{3} < 1\), the sum to infinity exists.
Sum to infinity, \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{5}{1-\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{5}{\frac{1}{3}} = 15\) (Ans.)
---"}]

question: CQ:A = p + p^2q + p^3q^2 + ..... is an infinite geometric series, and B = 2 + 22 + 222 + ..... [1766667948694]
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Express 5.123 in rational fraction.","marks":0,"answer":"5.123 = 5.123123123......
\[=5+(0.123+0.000123+0.000000123+....)\]
Here, the series in the parentheses is an infinite series.
Its first term, \( a=0.123 \)
common ratio, \( r=\frac{0.000123}{0.123} = 0.001 \)
\[\therefore 5.123=5+\frac{a}{1-r}=5+\frac{0.123}{1-0.001}\]
\[=5+\frac{0.123}{0.999}=5+\frac{123}{999}\]
\[=5+\frac{41}{333}=\frac{1706}{333} \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"If p = (5x+1)^{-1} and q = 1, impose a condition on x under which the infinite series represented by A will have a sum to infinity and find that sum.","marks":0,"answer":"Given that, \( p=(5x+1)^{-1}, q=1 \) and
A = p + p^2q + p^3q^2 + ......
\[=(5x+1)^{-1}+(5x+1)^{-2}\cdot 1+(5x+1)^{-3}\cdot (1)^2+....\]
[Substituting the values of p and q]
\[\therefore A=\frac{1}{5x+1}+\frac{1}{(5x+1)^2}+\frac{1}{(5x+1)^3}+......\]
Here, first term of the series, \( a=\frac{1}{5x+1} \)
and common ratio, \( r=\frac{1/(5x+1)^2}{1/(5x+1)}=\frac{1}{5x+1} \)
‘A’ will have a sum up to infinity if \(|r|<1\).
That is
\[\left| \frac{1}{5x+1} \right| < 1\]
or, \(-1<\frac{1}{5x+1}<1\).
Either, \(-1<\frac{1}{5x+1}\) or, \(\frac{1}{5x+1}<1\)
or, \(-1 > 5x + 1\) or, \(5x + 1 > 1\)
or, \(5x + 1 < -1\) or, \(5x > 0\)
or, \(5x < -2\) : \(x > 0\)
∴ \(x < -\frac{2}{5}\)
∴ Sum up to infinity of the given series will exist if \(x < -\frac{2}{5}\) or \(x > 0\)
Now, sum up to infinity of the series,
\[S_{\infty} = \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{\frac{1}{5x+1}}{1-\frac{1}{5x+1}} = \frac{\frac{1}{5x+1}}{\frac{5x+1-1}{5x+1}} = \frac{1}{5x} \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the sum of the first n terms of the series represented by B.","marks":0,"answer":"Given that,
B = 2 + 22 + 222 + ......
Let, \(S_n = 2 + 22 + 222 + ...... + n^{th} \text{ term}\),
= 2(1 + 11 + 111 + ...... + \(n^{th} \text{ term}\))
= \(\frac{2}{9}(9 + 99 + 999 + ...... + n^{th} \text{ term})\)
\[= \frac{2}{9}\left((10-1)+(100-1)+(1000-1)+...n^{th}\text{term}\right)\]
\[= \frac{2}{9}\left((10+100+1000+......n^{th}\text{term})-(1+1+1+......n^{th}\text{term})\right)\]
\[= \frac{2}{9}\left((10^1+10^2+10^3+......n^{th}\text{term})\right)\]

\[= \frac{2}{9}\left(\frac{10}{9}(10^n-1)-n\right)\]
\[= \frac{20}{81}(10^n-1)-\frac{2n}{9} \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]
---"}]

question:
CQ:(i) 3(1 + 11 + 111 + ………..)
(ii) a + ap + ap^2 + ………is a geometric series.
Combining Chapters 5 & 7 [1766667952454]
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Find the discriminant of equation \(7x - 1 + 2x^2 = 0\).","marks":0,"answer":"Given equation, \(7x - 1 + 2x^2 = 0\)
or, \(2x^2 + 7x - 1 = 0\);
Comparing the equation with ax^2 + bx + c = 0, we get,
a = 2, b = 7 and c = -1
Discriminant of the equation, D = \(b^2 - 4ac\)
= \(7^2 - 4 \times 2 \times (-1)\)
= \(49 + 8 = 57\) (Ans.)"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Find the sum of the first n terms of the series no. (i).","marks":0,"answer":"Given series: 3(1 + 11 + 111 + ……….. + nth term)
= \(\frac{3}{9}\) (9 + 99 + 999 + ……….. + nth term)
= \(\frac{1}{3}\) ((10 - 1) + (100 - 1) + (1000 - 1) + …… + nth term)
= \(\frac{1}{3}\) ((10 + 100 + 1000 + ……… + nth term) - n)
= \(\frac{1}{3}\) (10 \(\cdot\) \(\left(\frac{10^n - 1}{10 - 1}\right)\) - n)
= \(\frac{1}{3}\) (\(\frac{10(10^n - 1)}{9}\) - n)
= \(\frac{10}{27}(10^n - 1) - \frac{n}{3}\)
Therefore, the sum of the first n terms is: \(S_n = \frac{10}{27}(10^n - 1) - \frac{n}{3}\) (Ans.)"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"If a = p = \(\frac{1}{2x + 3}\), then impose a condition on x under which the infinite series will have a sum to infinity and find that sum.","marks":0,"answer":"Given a = p = \(\frac{1}{2x + 3}\).
The infinite geometric series is: \(a + ap + ap^2 + …… = \frac{1}{2x+3} + \left(\frac{1}{2x+3}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{1}{2x+3}\right)^3 + ……\)
First term, \(a = \frac{1}{2x + 3}\)
Common ratio, \(r = \frac{1}{2x + 3}\)
The series will have a sum to infinity if \(|r| < 1\), i.e., \(\left|\frac{1}{2x + 3}\right| < 1\).
This implies \(-1 < \frac{1}{2x + 3} < 1\).
Solving:
From \(\frac{1}{2x + 3} < 1\): \(\frac{1}{2x + 3} - 1 < 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{1 - (2x+3)}{2x+3} < 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{-2x -2}{2x+3} < 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{x+1}{2x+3} > 0\).
From \(\frac{1}{2x + 3} > -1\): \(\frac{1}{2x + 3} + 1 > 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{1 + (2x+3)}{2x+3} > 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\frac{2x+4}{2x+3} > 0\).
Combining the conditions, the required condition is: \(x < -\frac{3}{2}\) or \(x > -1\).
Sum to infinity, \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r} = \frac{\frac{1}{2x+3}}{1 - \frac{1}{2x+3}} = \frac{\frac{1}{2x+3}}{\frac{2x+3-1}{2x+3}} = \frac{1}{2x+2} = \frac{1}{2(x+1)}\) (Ans.)
---"}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Find out the nature and type of the roots of \(2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0\).","marks":0,"answer":"Given equation, \(2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0\)
Discriminant, D = \(7^2 - 4 \times 2 \times 3 = 49 - 24 = 25 = 5^2\)
Here, the discriminant of the equation, D > 0 and is a perfect square number.
Roots of the equation are rational, unequal, and real numbers (Ans.)"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Find the sum of the first n terms of the series A.","marks":0,"answer":"Given that, A = 4 + 44 + 444 + ………...
= 4(1 + 11 + 111 + ……….. + nth term)
= \(\frac{4}{9}\) (9 + 99 + 999 + ……….. + nth term)
= \(\frac{4}{9}\) ((10 - 1) + (100 - 1) + (1000 - 1) + …… + nth term)
= \(\frac{4}{9}\) ((10 + 100 + 1000 + ……… + nth term) - n)
= \(\frac{4}{9}\) (10 \(\cdot\) \(\left(\frac{10^n - 1}{10 - 1}\right)\) - n)
= \(\frac{40}{81}\) (10^n - 1) - \(\frac{4}{9}\) n
Therefore, the sum of the first n terms of series A,
\[S_n = \frac{40}{81}(10^n - 1) - \frac{4}{9} n \quad \text{(Ans.)}\]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Impose a condition on x under which the infinite series S will have a sum (to infinity) and find that sum.","marks":0,"answer":"Given, series:
\[S = 2(3x - 5)^{-1} + 4(3x - 5)^{-2} + 8(3x - 5)^{-3} + ……...\]
= \(\frac{2}{3x - 5} + \frac{4}{(3x - 5)^2} + \frac{8}{(3x - 5)^3} + ……\) which is a geometric series.
The first term of the series, a = \(\frac{2}{3x - 5}\)
Common ratio, r = \(\frac{4/(3x-5)^2}{2/(3x-5)} = \frac{2}{3x - 5}\)
The series will have sum to infinity if \(|r| < 1\)
Therefore, \(\left|\frac{2}{3x - 5}\right| < 1\) or, \(-1 < \frac{2}{3x - 5} < 1\)
Either, \(\frac{2}{3x - 5} < 1\) or, \(\frac{2}{3x - 5} > -1\)
or, \(2 < 3x - 5\) or, \(2 > -(3x - 5)\)
or, \(3x - 5 > 2\) or, \(3x - 5 < -2\)
or, \(3x > 7\) or, \(3x < 3\)
∴ \(x > \frac{7}{3}\) or \(x < 1\)
Required condition: \(x > \frac{7}{3}\) or, \(x < 1\) (Ans.)
Sum to infinity, \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r} = \frac{\frac{2}{3x - 5}}{1 - \frac{2}{3x - 5}}\)
= \(\frac{2}{3x - 5} \div \frac{3x - 5 - 2}{3x - 5} = \frac{2}{3x - 5} \times \frac{3x - 5}{3x - 7} = \frac{2}{3x - 7}\) (Ans.)"}]
